title: Pepsiman
subtitle: A soft-drink mascot cannot stop running
summary: Pepsiman is KID's PlayStation action game, released in Japan on 4 March 1999. The advertising mascot runs automatically through streets, buildings and increasingly improbable emergencies while the player steers him around obstacles. The immediate task is to survive the route, collecting Pepsi cans and reaching people apparently in need of the drink. Its four stages combine an uncomplicated running game with an unusually committed promotional premise. Cars, pedestrians and construction equipment become practical hazards, while even the product's own delivery vehicles can obstruct the hero sent to distribute it.
body: Pepsiman is KID's PlayStation action game, released in Japan on 4 March 1999. The advertising mascot runs automatically through streets, buildings and increasingly improbable emergencies while the player steers him around obstacles. The immediate task is to survive the route, collecting Pepsi cans and reaching people apparently in need of the drink. Its four stages combine an uncomplicated running game with an unusually committed promotional premise. Cars, pedestrians and construction equipment become practical hazards, while even the product's own delivery vehicles can obstruct the hero sent to distribute it.

Running, dashing and different jumps provide the means of responding to the course. Checkpoints soften repeated mistakes, but each section introduces arrangements that must be recognised quickly. Some passages change the rules by placing Pepsiman on a skateboard or trapping him in a metal bin that reverses the controls. Large objects pursue him at the end of stages, turning the camera and the direction of danger into another variation. The player learns a route through repetition, anticipating the next response before the automatically advancing character reaches the point where it becomes necessary.

The small budget led to inexpensive live-action interludes featuring Mike Butters watching Pepsiman while consuming Pepsi and snacks. Kotaro Uchikoshi contributed to the game's visual production before becoming better known for his narrative games. Although a North American release was considered, Pepsiman remained a Japanese PlayStation title. Its commercial reception was modest, but its absurd premise later attracted a substantial cult following. The game's appeal comes from the consistency of that absurdity: a straightforward obstacle course is presented with the complete seriousness of a world whose every crisis can be answered by one branded superhero.
